name: encrypted_survey
description: Survey an extracted directory tree for ransomware candidates and say what was and was not read. A file is a CANDIDATE when its name ends in an extension that is not a known one after a known one, with anything between them (report.docx.locked, report.docx.id[AB12CD34].locked), or its first 64 KiB reads at 7.5 bits per byte or more; a compressed archive reads the same way, so a candidate is a lead and each row says why. The first `sample` candidates of more than 4096 bytes, in print order, are profiled: entropy of three 64 KiB windows (head, middle, end, with their offsets and lengths; they overlap in a small file and intermittent encryption can fall between them) and the last `tail_bytes` bytes. It does NOT measure how much of any file was encrypted, whether a file is whole, which family wrote it or when anything ran: `noncandidate` means only that neither heuristic matched, a file of 4096 bytes or less is `unmeasured` (it has no entropy measurement; one whose name already makes it a candidate stays a candidate, with entropy_unmeasured), a file it could not read is `read_failed`, and a file not read because the read budget was spent is `unmeasured`; each has its own count and bytes, and `complete` says `partial` with the reasons when anything was left out. Modification times are counted by hour twice (each table's overflow past its cap is counted on its own), for every regular file and for the candidates, as the filesystem's mtime as collected (an extraction or copy changes it), never as an execution time. Bytes shared by the sampled tails are an observation pending a reference match, not a family marker. Every path is printed through the rule ransom_note_scan uses: each directory component, and the name of a file named like a note (the pattern ransom_note_scan uses; listed in note_name_candidates when under 100000 bytes), is withheld when it holds an identifier-shaped token (a run of 8 or more letters and digits holding both, a run of 10 or more digits, a run of 8 or more letters that is not one word, a capitalised word, several capitalised words or all capitals, a run of 16 or more letters of one case, 8 or more pairs of hex digits joined by one character that is not a letter, a digit or a slash (a colon, a dash, a dot, an underscore, a space, a bracket; a neighbour of the run that is not a letter or a digit does not hide it, a letter or a digit glued to a pair makes that pair no pair), or groups of three or more digits joined by a space or a comma that hold 10 digits or more; a name is folded first: full-width forms, digits of any script, a full-width solidus as a separator, and no invisible character: format characters, combining marks, variation selectors, fillers) or a token, key or user-info the shared withholding rules find, in every row and in the root, and is counted once per printed path in paths_withheld; the extension of a file whose name is withheld is withheld with it (`appended_extension` says so, appended_extensions_withheld in coverage counts them, and they are not in the extension table). Every other file's name is printed as it is, in every row, in the census, in the skipped and failed lists (it is the evidence, and an identifier in it is printed), an encrypted file's included. A name that is withheld is replaced by one constant marker, so that nothing derived from it is printed: no length, no extension, no stem, and the place of the name among its siblings does not follow its text either (names that print alike, the withheld ones, come in an order drawn afresh every run, so a row, a note id, a finding id and the files a limit keeps are in that order, which differs between runs); the order of names that print alike is a keyed hash of the whole path, so the same name under two directories has two unrelated ranks. A second check, written apart from the rule, reads every string of the answer, of every page and of the census on its way out and replaces one that is still identifier-shaped by a marker, makes a complete answer partial and says where in `boundary`; the one thing it lets through is the name of an ordinary file, which is evidence. A size of 10 or more digits followed by `bytes` in the tool's own sentences (a reason, a status basis) is a number, not an identifier, and the type of an error (IsADirectoryError) is a word. Names of well-known directories (System32, SysWOW64, INetCache, INetCookies, INetHistory, MSOCache, PSReadLine, Framework, Framework64, SQLServer, GPUCache, DawnWebGPUCache, DawnGraphiteCache, GrShaderCache, IndexedDB, overlay2, datastore1) are printed in any case. The identifier shape is a guess and its rates were measured on random draws per shape as a directory name (5,000 for the first rule, 1,000 for the later classes). Printed whole (100%): a token of seven characters or fewer, 8 or 9 decimal digits, groups of four joined by a dash, an underscore or a dot, two groups of 7 letters joined by a dash, up to 15 letters of one case (8 to 15 lower-case letters, 8 to 15 capitals), and a mix of Cyrillic look-alike letters and digits (99.9%); 7 pairs of hex digits joined by a colon, a dot or a space 100% (by a dash 29%), three groups of 3, 3 and 4 digits joined by a dash 100%, and 8 pairs of hex digits with a letter or a digit glued to a pair at an end of the run (the run then counts a pair fewer) 100% when the pairs are joined by a colon, a space or a dot (by a dash 3 to 15%). Printed some of the time: a random 8-character letters-and-digits token 3.3% (9 characters 2.2%, 12 characters 0.6%, 16 characters 0.1%), 8 lower-case letters and digits 7.1%, 12 full-width letters and digits 0.7%, and mixed-case letters (40,000 draws each) 12 characters 5.8%, 16 characters 2.4%, 24 characters 0.5%. Not printed (0 of 1,000): hex of 16, 32 or 64 characters, 12 or 20 decimal digits, 12 digits of another script, a UUID, base58 of 22 characters, base32 of 16 characters, 16 or more letters of one case, hex, 12 digits and 12 letters-and-digits split by invisible characters (format characters, combining marks, variation selectors, fillers: 0 of 7,875 each, in the middle and at an end), 8 pairs of hex digits joined by a colon, a dash, a dot or a space (also inside brackets, after an equals sign or in parentheses: id[aa-bb-...], key=aa:bb:...), and three groups of four digits joined by a space or a comma. The 16-letter rule has a cost: on 1,314,483 real directory components of another developer machine (150,000 directories) the rule withheld 5.5% of the components and some component of 40.0% of the directories before it and 5.8% and 41.8% with it (appletvsimulator and managedapplications are withheld with the 32-letter Chrome extension ids it is meant to catch). On a developer machine's application, cache and package trees the rule before it withheld 4.9% of 600,000 real directory components (dates, versions and package ids hold digits among letters) and some component of 38% of their directories, so a harmless name is often withheld: list the directory for it. Names are judged by shape only, by a deny-list of shapes that is not finite: an identifier of another shape is printed, and a new shape found is one more that was. Printed whole too (100% of 1,000 draws each unless a rate is given, as a directory name and as a file name; measured with the scan's copy of the rule, which a test holds equal to the survey's): 8 or more pairs of hex digits joined by a separator of two characters or more (a comma and a space, two colons, a dash with a space on each side, `][`, `)(`, `0xAA,0xBB`, every pair in brackets; two dashes 19%); 7 pairs joined by a no-break or an ideographic space or a comma (by an underscore or a percent sign 28 to 29%); a 6-pair MAC address with colons or dashes, a Cisco one (aabb.ccdd.eeff), an IPv6 address; digits in other groupings: 3, 3 and 4 joined by a dot, an underscore or an apostrophe, 1.234.567.890.123, two groups of 6 digits or 12 single digits joined by a dot, a dash, an underscore or an apostrophe, pairs of digits joined by a space or a comma; 5 groups of 5 or 3 groups of 7 letters or digits joined by a space, 4 groups of 6 joined by a dot, three groups of 7 letters joined by a dash, base32 in groups of 4 joined by a space, two 7-digit hex tokens joined by a dot or a dash; 16 CJK ideographs, emoji, a mix of Greek look-alike letters (99%), words joined by a dash; eight two-digit-hex directories one under another, and 4 pairs in a directory with 4 in the file name (a run of pairs is read within one path component). The second check reads the same shapes, so it holds the same classes. It reads only regular files, follows no link, walks in print order (directories and names ordered by the text printed for them, the withheld ones in an order drawn afresh every run, so which candidates fall in `sample` differs between runs) and skips a top-level proc, sys or dev (exclude_top_level_dirs) saying so; every exclusion, link, special file and failure is listed. The census (one row per entry, ending in a receipt row), every candidate and every table longer than `limit` are written whole as JSON Lines under tool-output and named in pages. It takes a directory tree, so it has no `use` triggers. Exit 0 means the survey ran; `status` (also `complete`) says `complete` or `partial`, with `status_basis`: partial also when candidates were left unprofiled by the `sample` limit, a table was capped, or the time limit (max_seconds, default 780, below the manifest's 900) stopped the walk, which names how many entries and directories were not examined. Thresholds compare the unrounded entropy (a head of 7.4996 prints as 7.5 and is not a candidate). A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted, exit code 128 + the signal) after removing the census and pages it was writing. A census or page file already there is never replaced, even by a rerun with other limits: the new one takes the next free name (`-2`, `-3`) and the answer names it. SIGKILL cannot be caught: a tool killed that way (the job service's last resort after its grace period) leaves the hidden temporary files of the census and the pages in tool-output, named by no answer and holding only rows already read back by the second check, and, in a window of microseconds, an empty file at a result name; delete them. The job's own timeout_seconds (default 900 for the survey, 600 for the scan) is not passed to the tool: give max_seconds a value below it, because a job stopped by its timeout answers failed, not partial.

root.description: A directory to survey (an extracted tree, not an image)

sample.description: Maximum number of candidate files of more than 4096 bytes to profile (head, middle and end windows, and a trailing-byte sample); default 200, at most 10000. Files are not read in full, and the selection is not random: the first candidates in print order (the withheld names in an order drawn afresh every run). Candidates beyond it are listed as not profiled (sample_limit)

tail_bytes.description: Trailing bytes to report per profiled candidate (default 32, 0 to 1024). They are raw bytes of the file

limit.description: Rows shown inline per table (default 200); every row is counted, and a table with more is written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages.<table>.all_results

read_budget_bytes.description: The most this survey reads in all, head windows and profiles together (default 4294967296, at least 4096). When it is spent the remaining files are `unmeasured` (read_budget_spent) and the survey is partial; raise it for a larger tree

exclude_top_level_dirs.description: Directory names skipped at the top of the root only (default ["proc", "sys", "dev"]: the pseudo-filesystems of a Linux root). Each is listed as an exclusion; [] excludes nothing, and a directory of that name deeper in the tree is always read

census.description: Write a row for every file visited (default true). false keeps rows for candidates, unmeasured and unreadable files and every entry skipped, excluded or not read, and counts the files that matched nothing

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 780, at most 840; the manifest's timeout is 900). When it runs out the walk stops, what was counted is written, and the answer is partial and says how many entries and directories were not examined
